page: Amazon Web Services c5n.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz, with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 21.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.62 GB of memory per core. It has no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core CPU performance and average memory bandwidth across both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks. Single-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% in stress-ng tests. While the instance achieves average scores in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, its multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and multi-core Geekbench scores are weak. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 7B model rated as poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for network-intensive workloads without the overhead of local storage. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations. It is less suitable for memory-heavy databases, large-scale LLM inference, or tasks requiring high single-core performance.
